correctness.rationale: Correct for the pure Fraisse-limit theory DMT of meet-trees in the order/meet language. For nonempty finite P, A=dcl(P) is exactly the finite meet closure, and A being term-definable from P gives the same 1-type space. The one-point generation lemma gives <A,b>=A union {b,c}, where c=max_{a in A}(a meet b), with at most one c outside A. By quantifier elimination, a complete 1-type is exactly its finite meet/order diagram over A. For m=|A|, algebraic types number m. For nonalgebraic b=c, its cut inserts b either below the minimum of A or in one of the m-1 cover edges, giving m types. For c in A and b>c, b uses one fresh cone over each possible old c, giving m types. For c not in A and b>c, c is in the same m gaps and b uses a fresh cone at c, giving m more types; c cannot lie above an old maximal vertex since then it would not be a meet with A. Density and infinite ramification realize every signature, homogeneity and QE make each signature a single type, so |S_1(P)|=m+3m=4m. An n-point generating set produces at most one extra maximal meet point when each next generator is adjoined, so n<=|dcl(P)|<=2n-1; an n-chain and n leaves of a finite full binary meet-tree attain the endpoints. Thus 4n<=|S_1(P)|<=8n-4 for n>=1, maximum 8n-4; S_1(empty)=1 by transitivity. Independent exact combinatorial enumeration, not a general proof, confirmed 3m nonalgebraic signatures for every finite meet-closed labeled base through m=4 and the closure inequality across 510293 subsets of rooted trees through six vertices.
